claims.object_text: infantile-onset epilepsy and severe intellectual disability in girls
claims.quote: Pathogenic truncating variants in SMC1A, which is located on chromosome Xp11.2, are known to cause infantile-onset epilepsy and severe intellectual disability in girls.
Several studies have reported a correlation between SMC1A truncations and seizure clustering;

claims.object_text: mild abnormality in the interictal EEG during infancy and early childhood
claims.quote: Our patient presented with a mild abnormality in the interictal EEG during infancy and early childhood despite frequent seizure clustering.
Notably, the patient's EEG findings gradually deteriorated over time, which was inconsistent with the amelioration of seizure clustering.

claims.object_text: tonic-clonic seizures occurring in clusters several times a week
claims.quote: The patient experienced unknown onset, tonic-clonic seizures that occurred in clusters several times a week.
had developed epilepsy at the age of 4 months.

claims.object_text: no seizure clustering since age 9 years
claims.quote: the patient did not experience seizure clustering since the age of 9 years.
